Can you explain the main options in simple terms?
• Just now
Seen • Just now
Here’s a simple starting point:
Whiskey — aged and often warming; Bourbon tends toward vanilla and caramel, Rye is spicier, and Scotch can range from fruity to smoky. Whiskey is commonly bottled around 40–46% ABV.
Tequila — made from agave; often bright and earthy. Great in cocktails, with aged styles offering a smoother, richer sip.
Rum — typically associated with Caribbean and South American traditions; it can be light and easy for cocktails or richer when aged. Most rum is bottled around 40% ABV.
Gin — botanical and aromatic, usually led by juniper; ideal if you enjoy fresh, herbal, citrusy drinks.
Vodka — clear and neutral in style, making it especially versatile for mixed drinks.
Brandy — fruit-based and often smooth, warming, and rich.
Flaviar carries whiskey, rum, gin, tequila, vodka, brandy, and more, including approachable classics and craft bottles.

• Just now
Seen • Just now
For your first taste, keep it simple:
Pour a small amount into any clean tumbler or short glass.
Take a gentle smell first—don’t put your nose deep into the glass.
Take a small sip and let it sit on your tongue for a moment before swallowing.
If it feels too strong, add a small splash of water; this can soften the spice and bring out Four Roses’ honey and vanilla notes.
If you prefer it chilled, add one large ice cube rather than lots of small cubes, so it dilutes more slowly. 
You can also taste it neat first, then decide whether water or ice suits you better—there’s no wrong way to enjoy it.
